overall: Atlanta is in the pre-dawn hours with a current temperature of 64.4°F and a running max of 69.8°F set just after midnight; since then temperatures have drifted lower at a rate of about -1.8°F/hr. forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show moderate spread: HRRR is the warmest at 87.5°F, while ECMWF and NBM both land at 84.8°F — a ~2.7°F gap. The NWS official forecast of 87°F aligns closely with HRRR and sits above the ECMWF/NBM consensus, suggesting the operational forecast leans on the warmer solution. The META (fused) model distribution places 35.4% probability each in the 86-87°F and 88-89°F buckets, with 19.9% in 90-91°F, effectively centering around 87-88°F and confirming the NWS/HRRR signal rather than the cooler ECMWF/NBM guidance.
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence points to a high in the 86-88°F range. Mostly sunny skies, very light winds, and a mild overnight low around 64°F support efficient daytime heating toward the NWS target of 87°F; the warm-biased HRRR at 87.5°F and the META distribution centered on 87-88°F reinforce this. Confidence is moderate-to-good — models agree directionally but the 2-3°F spread between ECMWF/NBM and HRRR/NWS introduces some uncertainty, and the peak is expected near 4-5 PM ET.
